data.name: Nawazish
data.gender_notes: Nawazish is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘nawwaza’, meaning ‘to give’ or ‘to bestow’. This name signifies the one who is generous in giving and receives blessings in return. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said: ‘The believer’s shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his charity.’ (Sahih Muslim). The name Nawazish carries the meaning “Gifted, Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nawazish usually hope their child will grow to embody gifted, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace generosity, as it is a virtue that opens doors to Allah's blessings.
data.etymology: Nawazish belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gifted, Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nawazish total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

This grant, called Nawazish, was a significant source of power and wealth for the Ansari family and helped establish them as influential landlords in the region.

Nawab Nawazish Ali Khan, a prominent Nawab (noble) of the princely state of Rampur in North India during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, was known for his military prowess and political acumen. The title 'Nawab Nawazish Ali Khan' was bestowed upon him by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in the early 17th century as a mark of recognition for his family's loyalty and military services to the empire.
